findings.body:
twa (540910e09) binds runner pi-durable for every profile dispatching into Cloudflare, but the e2e fixtures still declare the cloudflare-sandbox KnownExecutor with Runners ["pi"], so usableProfile refuses every run ('profile implement-tick names runner "pi-durable" for executor cloudflare-sandbox, which launches pi'). The tests call shorttest.EndToEnd, so the per-tick integrated gate skipped them; CI on epic/43y has been red on reconcile shards 1-3 since 15:25 UTC (runs 37332698366..37340930478; last green d7ca3e572). Reproduced locally at HEAD. Fix: fixtures use profile.CloudRule.Harnesses (as internal/cli/executor.go:82 does) or include pi-durable; then CI on the epic head must be green.
evidence: internal/reconcile/sandbox_adoption_test.go:625 and substrate_routing_test.go:183 (Runners: []string{"pi"}); internal/reconcile/profiles.go:516; gh run view 37340930478 --log-failed
findings.title: Full Go suite red: 7 reconcile e2e fixtures still declare cloud runner pi

findings.body:
The only recorded staging result for A2's second fault is the pre-a2l shape: the workspace was emptied, the container was not destroyed. The README itself says the destroy is 'to be re-run at the next staging pass'. The code a2l added for a real destroy (the staging Worker's /proof/git origin, the dumb-HTTP origin, /proof/destroy) has never run on the platform. cni's restore-setup proof also only empties the workspace. Fix: run agent-faults-staging.ts with the whole-container destroy and record the result table. Staging deploys from the branch, so this need not wait for the merge.
evidence: harness/proof/README.md:231-236; harness/proof/README.md recorded table rows 'Workspace lost mid-turn'
findings.title: A2's container-destroyed-mid-turn proof was never run on staging after a2l

findings.body:
The local real-run record explicitly disclaims the mid-tool kill and container-loss proofs, and the post-merge cloud runbook (kkt) scores only A4. Nothing records a harness kill or a container loss inside a real epic run. Either inject a local harness kill mid-tool during a real local run, or extend docs/pi-durable-cloud-run-runbook.md so the post-merge cloud run observes and records A2's real-run half. Otherwise the close-out should score A2's real-run clause as predicted.
evidence: docs/pi-durable-local-epic-run-2026-10-05.md 'Does not claim'; docs/pi-durable-cloud-run-runbook.md (A4 only)
findings.title: A2's 'proven in a real run' has no evidence for either fault

findings.body:
restoreWorkspace treats any non-zero exit of 'git fetch origin $BRANCH' as 'the branch does not exist yet' and restores at the base. That includes a forge 5xx, a network blip or a token-door hiccup. The next round's pushWipCheckpoint does 'git push -f' to the attempt branch, overwriting every earlier wip snapshot and the agent's commits. A transient failure during a restore therefore silently loses the attempt's work. Distinguish a missing ref (git ls-remote) from a failed fetch, and fail the restore on the latter.
evidence: harness/src/workspace/checkpoints.ts:383-388 (fallback), :237 (git push -f)
findings.title: Restore falls back to base on any branch-fetch failure, then force-push wipes it

findings.body:
The boot runs configure_caches, provision_toolchain and worker_repo_setup. The restore's setup entry (run_setup_entry) runs only configure_caches and worker_repo_setup. A repository that declares a toolchain the image lacks (mise.toml, .tool-versions) gets it at boot, but not after a container loss, so tests on the restored tree fail.
evidence: image/worker.sh:1527-1541 vs :1460-1493; image/common.sh:1067
findings.title: Restore's setup entry skips provision_toolchain; a restored box lacks mise tools

findings.body:
sandboxExecutor passes no StuckAfter, and internal/exec/cloudflaresandbox has no stuck logic. The WorkerAgent's steer is reached only by the operator routes, although worker-attempt.ts and sandbox-dispatch.ts both say 'the stuck nudge is one of these'. A cloud attempt stuck on a hung bash (pi-durable's bash has no default timeout) runs to its wall deadline. This is not a regression, since main had no cloud nudge, but A3's 'the stuck nudge is a steer' holds only locally.
evidence: internal/cli/executor.go:185-209; harness/src/host/worker-attempt.ts:349; cloudflare/src/sandbox-dispatch.ts:882
findings.title: No stuck nudge for cloud pi-durable workers; A3's nudge clause is local-only

findings.body:
LastStorageEvent stats worker.sqlite. pi-durable 1.0.2 opens node SQLite with journal_mode=WAL and wal_autocheckpoint=1000, so commits land in worker.sqlite-wal and the main file's mtime stays put until a checkpoint. The conversation therefore barely counts as an activity signal. A worker that is thinking or reading for a long time is steered as stuck, and later stopped. Stat the -wal file too, or use the newer of the two.
evidence: internal/exec/subprocess/activity.go:324-331; pi-durable dist/storage/sqlite/node.js:160-162
findings.title: Durable runner activity reads worker.sqlite mtime, but pi-durable writes WAL

findings.body:
On a delivered steer, the supervisor breaks out without interrupting the tool tree. A steer is placed after the current tool round, and a hung bash round never ends, so DecideStuck returns StuckStop one StuckAfter later. The old CLI path killed the tool processes and re-prompted, which recovered the worker. steer_test.go:213 asserts the new stop outcome. Consider interrupting the running tool when the evidence is a hung tool.
evidence: internal/exec/subprocess/supervisor.go:287-297; internal/exec/subprocess/steer_test.go:213
findings.title: Local stuck steer cannot reach a hung tool; attempt is stopped, not recovered

findings.body:
Tick 8em closed A1's cloud PR-review gap by appending a note to epic 43y that declares the omp review boot an exception 'now on the record'. The operator's recorded exceptions cover only the local claude rung (and the j6o review/closeout blessing). A worker-authored exception to an acceptance item should be confirmed by the operator at close-out, or the review boot moved onto pi-durable.
evidence: .tick/issues/43y.json notes 2026-10-05 18:25; cloudflare/src/worker-boot.ts:504,529; cloudflare/src/run-workflow.ts:1756
findings.title: Cloud PR-review omp exception to A1 was recorded by a worker, not the operator

findings.body:
When the tree equals HEAD and no ticfac-wip-pushed record exists, pushWipCheckpoint writes the record and exits 3 without pushing, assuming HEAD is on origin. After a restore (which deletes .git's record) or a round-1 commit, HEAD has moved past origin, so the agent's commits are not pushed. A further container loss restores the older tip.
evidence: harness/src/workspace/checkpoints.ts:215-216
findings.title: First clean wip round is recorded as pushed without a push; commits can be lost

findings.body:
FactorySandbox.listProcesses returns nothing while the in-memory ready flag is false, as it is after a deploy restarts the DO. Tracked bash's resume then misses the live process and starts the command again. Today ensureGuard's door.run sets ready first; with guardDir null (a supported option) the tool would run twice. The resume tests use guardDir null with fakes that do not model ready.
evidence: cloudflare/src/factory-sandbox.ts:597; harness/src/env/factory-sandbox.ts:758,774-786; harness/test/tracked-bash-resume.test.ts
findings.title: Nonce replay relies on ensureGuard marking FactorySandbox ready first

findings.body:
The kill scenario's last claim matches /wip checkpoint … pushed/ anywhere in the log, so a checkpoint from before the kill satisfies it. The README's 'four … after the resume' was read by hand.
evidence: harness/proof/agent-faults-staging.ts (kill scenario, last claim)
findings.title: agent-faults proof's 'checkpoints after the resume' claim is not order-checked
